newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar to retain bullishness vs yen in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Dollar to retain bullishness vs yen in Asia.

text.p: The dollar is seen maintaining its bullish trend in Asia on Thursday, with operators more eager to build up long positions on the greenback's fall against the yen, dealers said.
Dealers will determine specific direction for dollar/yen from Japanese June trade figures due for release at 2350 GMT.

"We need to see the outcome of the trade figures before taking new positions, but it seems Tokyo operators are become more keen about building up long positions," a Japanese trust bank dealer said. "At this stage, I don't see many dollar-long positions piling up in the market."
Economists' forecasts for Japan's June trade surplus ranged from 971.0 billion yen to 1.61 trillion yen, or a rise of between 33 percent to 120 percent from a year earlier.
"A trade surplus of about 1.5 trillion yen could surprise the market and trigger active selling of the dollar, but otherwise operators are expected to hunt dollars on dips," the dealer said.
Meanwhile, a city bank dealer said the dollar could be locked in a tight range if the trade surplus is in line with the market consensus of about 1.0 to 1.1 trillion yen.

"A wait-and-see attitude could dominate the market if the trade figures are in line with the forecasts. The market will then look towards U.S. trade figures (due for release on Friday)," the city bank dealer said.

Japanese institutional investors, who have been selling dollars to hedge risks for their U.S. Treasury holdings, were now keen to unwind those short positions as the dollar was unlikely to dip sharply from current levels, dealers said.
Dealers said the dollar is expected to find support around 114.80/90 yen, while Japanese exporters are showing dollar-selling interest near 116 yen.
Although the dollar fell from its high against the mark overnight in New York, dealers were still not eager about buying back the mark aggressively.

German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said the dollar and British pound had risen against the German mark because of strong economies in the United States and Britain and that currency market fluctuations were no grounds for worry.
The comments from Waigel and other German officials were far more optimistic than investors had expected.
Dealers expect the dollar to move in a range of 1.7870 to 1.7980 marks in Asia.
